title: Automating Escrow with USDC and AI - Corey Cooper, Circle
talk_summary: A Circle DevRel lead demos an open-source escrow agent that parses a PDF agreement with a multimodal LLM into JSON, deploys a templated Solidity escrow contract via Circle APIs, and has an agent verify deliverables and release USDC. The only transferable engineering content is the human-in-the-loop review pattern for non-deterministic LLM output and the structured-JSON extraction step.

takeaways.technique: Human-in-the-loop gate on non-deterministic LLM output
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent parses the agreement and proposes a listing (amount, deliverables), but a human must approve it before the contract is deployed; the agent only recommends, the person is the final approver.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the best safest way to design these experiences is with human in the loop built into it ... you're the final approver

takeaways.technique: Schema-constrained JSON extraction from unstructured docs
takeaways.what_they_do: They prompt the model to emit a fixed JSON schema (amount, task list) so downstream code can consume it deterministically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've created a prompt to make sure it outputs it in JSON ... outputs it in kind of a JSON format

takeaways.what_they_do: Proposes CFO/controller/accountant agents cross-checking each other's work, requiring multi-signature approval above a dollar threshold.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a CFO agent, a controller agent, accountant agent, and those agents are cross-checking each other's work

takeaways.technique: Contract-factory / template reuse to cut per-instance cost
takeaways.what_they_do: They deploy a template contract repeatedly via API rather than authoring per case, and mention a factory pattern to reduce gas per deployment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can actually deploy like a contract factory ... to be more efficient on the gas
